value.rationale: The Gaussian pure Landau disk problem naturally asks how strongly Hermite-index ordering can fail, because finite Weyl–Heisenberg approximations use selected eigenspaces. The result gives, for every previously unclassified higher \(q\ge3\), exactly 2q (or 2k+1) simple radial order exchanges per adjacent pair, an all-radius sharp q-ascent bound over infinitely many modes, and Hermite-root positions of all possible turning points. This is an all-level structural classification rather than a low-degree isolated computation or a restatement of the known eigenvalue integrals.
